### Q1. JEE Main 2022 (25 Jul Shift 2)

*Type:* `numerical` | *Difficulty Level:* `1`

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>56</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>&#160;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> of nitrogen gas is mixed with excess of hydrogen gas and it is found that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>&#160;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> of ammonia gas is produced, The volume of unused nitrogen gas is found to be_____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math>.

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Value:** **46**

**Detailed Solution:**

<p><img src="https://cdn-question-pool.getmarks.app/pyq/jee_main/32d363e8-db0a-43c3-a183-9a0dc7db6758-image.png" style="width: 316px; height: 100px;" /></p><p>Gay-Lussac&#39;s Law proposes a relationship between the combining volumes of gases with respect to the reactants and gaseous products. ### Q2. JEE Main 2022 (26 Jun Shift 2)

*Type:* `numerical` | *Difficulty Level:* `1`

The moles of methane required to produce <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>81</mn><mo>&#160;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of water after complete combustion is____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>&#215;</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&#160;</mo><mi>mol</mi></math>. [nearest integer]

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Value:** **225**

**Detailed Solution:**

<p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CH</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&#10230;</mo><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></math></p><p>POAC on H atom</p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>nCH</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>nH</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>2</mn></math></p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>nCH</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>81</mn><mn>18</mn></mfrac><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>81</mn><mn>36</mn></mfrac></math></p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>nCH</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn></math></p><p><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>225</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math></p><p>Hence, the number of moles of methane is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>225</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math></p>

### Q6. JEE Main 2020 (07 Jan Shift 1)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Difficulty Level:* `1`

Amongst the following statements, that which was not proposed by Dalton was :

**Options:**

- **(A)** chemical reactions involve reorganization of atoms. These are neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
- **(B)** all the atoms of a given element have identical properties including identical mass. Atoms of different elements differ in mass.
- **(C)** when gases combine or reproduced in a chemical reaction they do so in a simple ratio by volume provided all gases are at the same T &amp; P.
- **(D)** matter consists of indivisible atoms.

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(C) when gases combine or reproduced in a chemical reaction they do so in a simple ratio by volume provided all gases are at the same T &amp; P.**

**Detailed Solution:**

When gases combine or reproduced in a chemical reaction they do so in a simple ratio by volume provided all gases are at the same T &amp; P.

</details>

- **(B)** 7 : 32
- **(C)** 1 : 8
- **(D)** 3 : 16

<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(B) 7 : 32**

**Detailed Solution:**

<blockquote><p>Let the mass of oxygen be <math><mi>x</mi></math> gm
<math> <mrow> <mo>&#8756;&#160;&#160;</mo> </mrow> </math> Mass of nitrogen = <math><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></math> gm
Number of molecules = 6.023 x 10<sup>23</sup> x number of moles
<math> <mrow> <mo>&#8756;&#160;&#160;</mo> <mtext>Ratio</mtext> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <mtext>6.023</mtext> <mo>&#215;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <msup> <mn>0</mn> <mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mn>3</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mo>&#215;</mo> <mtext>no. of moles of oxygen</mtext> </mrow> <mrow> <mtext>6.023</mtext> <mo>&#215;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <msup> <mn>0</mn> <mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mn>3</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mo>&#215;</mo> <mtext>no. of moles of nitrogen</mtext> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> </math>
              <math> <mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <mfrac> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>m</mtext> <msub> <mtext>O</mtext> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </msub> </mrow> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>M</mtext> <msub> <mtext>O</mtext> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </msub> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> <mrow> <mfrac> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>m</mtext> <msub> <mtext>N</mtext> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </msub> </mrow> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>M</mtext> <msub> <mtext>N</mtext> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </msub> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> </mfrac> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <mfrac> <mrow> <mi>x</mi> </mrow> <mrow> <mn>3</mn> <mn>2</mn> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> <mrow> <mfrac> <mrow> <mn>4</mn> <mi>x</mi> </mrow> <mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mn>8</mn> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> </mfrac> </mrow> </math>
              <math> <mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <mn>7</mn> </mrow> <mrow> <mn>3</mn> <mn>2</mn> </mrow> </mfrac> <mo>=</mo> <mtext>7 : 32</mtext> </mrow> </math></p></blockquote>

### Q8. JEE Main 2012 (19 May Online)

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Difficulty Level:* `3`

When $\mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}$ is passed over red hot coke it partially gets reduced to $\mathrm{CO}(g)$. Upon passing $0.5 \mathrm{~L}$ of $\mathrm{CO}_2(g)$ over red hot coke, the total volume of the gases increased to $700 \mathrm{~mL}$. The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is

**Options:**

- **(A)** $\mathrm{CO}_2=300 \mathrm{~mL} ; \mathrm{CO}=400 \mathrm{~mL}$
- **(B)** $\mathrm{CO}_2=0.0 \mathrm{~mL} ; \mathrm{CO}=700 \mathrm{~mL}$
- **(C)** $\mathrm{CO}_2=200 \mathrm{~mL} ; \mathrm{CO}=500 \mathrm{~mL}$
- **(D)** $\mathrm{CO}_2=350 \mathrm{~mL} ; \mathrm{CO}=350 \mathrm{~mL}$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(A) $\mathrm{CO}_2=300 \mathrm{~mL} ; \mathrm{CO}=400 \mathrm{~mL}$**

**Detailed Solution:**

$\mathrm{CO}_2+\mathrm{C} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO}$
Stoichoimetry ratio is $1: 2$
AT STP, $P=1 \mathrm{~atm}, T=273 \mathrm{~K}, R=0.0821$
Initial moles of $\mathrm{CO}_2 ; n\left(\mathrm{CO}_2\right.$ initial $)=\frac{P V}{R T}$ $=\frac{1 \times 0.5}{0.0821 \times 273}=0.022 \mathrm{~mole}$
In final mixture no. of moles; $n\left(\mathrm{CO}_2 / \mathrm{CO}\right.$ mixture)
$$
=\frac{1 \times 0.7}{0.0821 \times 273}=0.031
$$
Increase in volume is by $=0.031-0.022$ $=0.009$ mole of gas
Final no. of moles of $\mathrm{CO}$ i.e. $n_{\text {(CO final) }}$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& n_{\text {(CO final) }}=2 n_{\left(\mathrm{CO}_2 \text { initial }\right)}-n_{\left(\mathrm{CO}_2\right. \text { final) }} \\
& \quad=2\left(0.022-\mathrm{n}_{\left(\mathrm{CO}_2 \text { final }\right)}\right. \\
& \left.n_{\text {(CO final) }}=0.044-2 n_{\text {(CO }} \text { final }\right) \\
& \therefore \text { Now, } n_{\text {(CO final) }}+n_{\text {(CO final) }}=0.031 \\
& n_{\left(\mathrm{CO}_2\right. \text { final) }}=0.031-n_{\text {(CO final) })} \ldots \text { (iii) }
\end{aligned}
$$
Substituting (ii) in eq. (i)
$$
\begin{aligned}
& n_{\text {(CO final) }}=0.044-2\left[0.031-n_{\text {(CO final) }}\right. \\
& n_{\text {(CO final) }}=0.044-0.062+2 n_{\text {(CO final })}
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
n_{(\mathrm{CO} \text { final) }}=0.018 \mathrm{~mol} .
$$
Volume of $\mathrm{CO}=V=\frac{n R T}{P}=\frac{0.018 \times 0.0821 \times 273}{1}$ $=0.40$ Litre
and volume of $\mathrm{CO}_2=0.7$ litre $-0.4$ litre $=0.3$ litre
$$
\therefore \mathrm{CO}_2=300 \mathrm{~mL}, \mathrm{CO}=400 \mathrm{~mL}
$$

</details>

### Q10. JEE Main 2003

*Type:* `singleCorrect` | *Difficulty Level:* `2`

What volume of hydrogen gas, at $273 \mathrm{~K}$ and $1 \mathrm{~atm}$, pressure will be consumed in obtaining $21.6 \mathrm{~g}$ of elemental boron (atomic mass $=10.8$ ) from the reducti on of boron trichloride by hydrogen?

**Options:**

- **(A)** $67.2 \mathrm{~L}$
- **(B)** $44.8 \mathrm{~L}$
- **(C)** $22.4 \mathrm{~L}$
- **(D)** $89.6 \mathrm{~L}$

<details>
<summary><b>View Answer & Solution</b></summary>

**Correct Option:** **(A) $67.2 \mathrm{~L}$**

**Detailed Solution:**

No. of moles of boron $=\frac{21.6}{10.8}=2$
for $\mathrm{BCl}_3$
$\therefore 1$ mole of Boron $=3$ mole of $\mathrm{Cl}$
$\therefore 2$ mole of Boron $=6$ mole of $\mathrm{Cl}$
$\mathrm{H}_2+\mathrm{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{HCI}$
$\Rightarrow 3$ moles of Hydrogen is required
$=3 \times 22.4=67.2$ Litre

</details>
